subject: Ops tide-check: OKR crosswalk + QBR dry-run asks
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ops tide-check: OKR crosswalk + QBR dry-run asks

Morning team — short tide-check ahead of next week's QBR dry-run. TL;DR: good momentum on capacity/latency OKRs, one spike in request drop-rate on Dedicated, and three asks for exec support.

Wins
- Serving runtime: merged kernel-selection optimization reduced p50 generation latency by ~8% on standard workloads (benchmark attached).
- Redwood Dedicated onboarding: ApexHealth pilot scheduled for Tuesday; initial throughput tests met committed tps at 90% utilization.
- Console telemetry: token-level billing per-route rollout complete for all internal customers.

Risks / Gaps
- Request drop-rate: observed intermittent drops on Dedicated when autoscaler triggers pod churn during multi-tenant bursts; root cause likely race in cache warmup. Impact: several customer p99s spiking for 30–90s windows.
- QBR readiness: runbook needs a dry-run and final roles assigned — some slides still missing owner annotations.
- Sales / legal: ApexHealth requested a minor SSO/SCIM clarification and an updated SOC-2 evidence snippet (see external thread attached).

Asks (action and owner suggested)
1) Engineering: prioritize a small rollback-safe change to the autoscaler warmup path — ETA 48 hours. Owner: Jonas (can you confirm?)
2) Product/CS: finalize QBR deck owners and a 60-minute dry-run slot. Owner: Marissa to coordinate with Laura for exec time.
3) Legal/Sales assist: provide SOC-2 artifact and a short note on data retention for ApexHealth — copy to contracts. Owner: Karthik to help expedite.

Attachments: QBR_runbook_v1.docx (docx), serving-kernel-benchmarks-Apr15.csv (csv), apex_sso_question.txt (txt).

Notes: I'll run the dry-run checklist Wednesday 11:00–12:00 PT if that works for leadership. If not, propose alternate slot.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
(Attachment: QBR_runbook_v1.docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops tide-check: OKR crosswalk + QBR dry-run asks

Thanks Priya — solid summary. Quick Qs: 
- Jonas: do we have a short mitigation (config) we can ship today to reduce drop-rate while you investigate the warmup race? If yes, call it out so we can notify impacted customers.
- Marissa: for the dry-run, can you confirm whether execs want the customer deep-dive (ApexHealth) included in the internal rehearsal or kept to the external slot?

Also flagging capacity: if we push the dry-run to Wednesday, engineering leads should be informed by EOD today so they can freeze non-critical deploys for the window.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product
(Attachment: none)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops tide-check: OKR crosswalk + QBR dry-run asks

Laura — good points. Quick updates inline and next steps.

On Mon, Apr 15, 2029 at 10:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Priya — solid summary. Quick Qs: 
> - Jonas: do we have a short mitigation (config) we can ship today to reduce drop-rate while you investigate the warmup race? If yes, call it out so we can notify impacted customers.

Jonas: recommendation from infra is a small change to the autoscaler delay (increase stabilization window from 10s -> 45s) and pre-warm a minimal cache on new pods. We believe this is rollback-safe and reduces the observed drop window. Can you confirm feasibility by EOD?

> - Marissa: for the dry-run, can you confirm whether execs want the customer deep-dive (ApexHealth) included in the internal rehearsal or kept to the external slot?

Marissa: suggest we keep the customer-facing portion out of the internal dry-run; do the internal run focusing on flow/roles, then do a separate 30-minute customer prep with ApexHealth on Thursday. Please confirm.

I updated the runbook draft and attached a PDF with owner annotations (QBR_runbook_v2.pdf). Also added the ApexHealth SCIM question under "pre-meeting asks" with the contact Rajiv (external).

Next steps (owners & times)
- Jonas: confirm autoscaler config change by EOD (engineering mitigation).
- Marissa: schedule internal dry-run Wed 11:00–12:00 PT and customer prep Thu 10:00–10:30 PT; confirm calendar invites.
- Karthik: hit up Nexia for the SOC-2 artifact and route to ApexHealth security.

(Attachment: QBR_runbook_v2.pdf)

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops tide-check: OKR crosswalk + QBR dry-run asks

Priya / team — I can take the autoscaler mitigation. Plan: push the stabilization-window increase and a lightweight cache-prewarm hook to canary tonight (0200 PT) and monitor for 72 hours. Rollback steps documented in the canary run notes. If metrics look stable, we'll promote to prod by tomorrow evening.

I'll own the customer notification draft (short status + expected ETA) and share by 17:00 PT for review.

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime
